heroTitle: Classified in Switzerland.|Documented for the EU.
intro: Two independent legal assessments by LEXR describe how ZCHF and the pool shares fit Swiss and EU law. This page summarises them; the documents themselves are linked below.

rows.title: Switzerland
rows.body: According to the assessment by LEXR Law Switzerland AG (August 2024), ZCHF qualifies as a payment token and a currency-linked stablecoin under FINMA's guidelines, not as a security, and using it to pay for goods and services is generally outside Swiss financial market law. The same assessment classifies the pool shares (FPS) as a utility token that gives access to governance.

rows.title: European Union
rows.body: According to the opinion by LEXR Germany Rechtsanwalts GmbH (February 2026), ZCHF is a crypto-asset under MiCA with no identifiable issuer, so the issuer duties of MiCA Titles II to IV do not apply to it. A MiCA-format white paper for ZCHF has been published and appears in ESMA's interim MiCA register. The register entry records the white paper; it is not an approval or endorsement by ESMA or any authority.

rows.title: Service providers
rows.body: Exchanges, custodians and other crypto-asset service providers that handle ZCHF remain subject to their own licensing, anti-money-laundering and consumer-protection obligations in their jurisdiction. The assessments describe the token, not the obligations of the businesses that offer it.
